4977375486314096411: Su Yuandao, a man who seemed to have become a symbol. No matter what happened, his reactions could always be perfectly anticipated by his junior disciples. What the "Eldest Senior Brother" should do, the "Eldest Senior Brother" would do. His righteousness and thoughtfulness appeared innate, and with him present, his diverse group of junior disciples always felt reassured. Yet no one is born to be the Eldest Senior Brother. He tucked his master, his junior disciples, and the entire sect bit by bit into his heart. When there was no more room, he began to carve out pieces of himself—little by little, again and again—until he became what he was now: the very embodiment of the title "Eldest Senior Brother." The process sounded painful, but Su Yuandao found joy in it. Because he had the finest master in the world, the finest four junior disciples, and above all, the finest Mohist Hill. And the finest Mohist Hill in the world would not stand idly by. "The imperial court is embroiled in infighting; Han eyes Chu's lands. Unrelated to the greater fate of the realm—we may observe and wait." When Wei Suifeng arrived with the secret missive from the Hengji Hall, Su Yuandao knew he was finally about to do something the "Eldest Senior Brother" should not. The Elders had their reasons, but Su Yuandao simply felt—this should not be the way. The third disciple’s face was scarred by war; the fifth’s Inner Demon remained unresolved even after twenty years. They had all become orphans in the flames of battle. Had they not been fortuitously taken into Hidden Mountain, none would have survived. Such good children—why should they not live? Sometimes Su Yuandao wondered, how could there be so many orphans in this world? Did this truly align with the Heavenly Way in the hearts of the Mohists? With the chaos now spreading in Southern Chu, how many more orphans would there be? How could this be "unrelated to the greater fate of the realm," and thus warrant mere observation? As he reined in his Horse and looked back, the Eldest Senior Brother knew that from this moment on, he would no longer be the esteemed disciple of the Pavilion of Myriad Forms, but a rebel of the Mohist Gate. Yet his eyes still gleamed as they fixed upon Mohist City— Farewell, Mohist Hill. My Mohist Hill. The finest Mohist Hill in the world.
